small_guidance:
- The torch ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime here (output is 128×16×31×63×63 ≈ 250M elements); the maxpool+GAP+clamp kernel is already trivial. Tuning BLOCK/num_warps on it cannot close the 2× gap.
- If staying with this structure, at least skip the intermediate `.contiguous()` (output of cuDNN convT is already contiguous) and switch the pool kernel to a 2D grid `(N, C)` so program lookup is cheaper, but expected gain is tiny.
- Add larger-BLOCK autotune configs (2048, 4096) and num_warps=16 since S = 15·31·31 ≈ 14k fits easily in one program.
large_guidance:
- Replace ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), compute the input×weight outer product and scatter-add into the output grid handling stride=2/padding=1. This is the heavy op (~250M output elements, 27·3·16 MAC per output) and has the most headroom.
- Fuse the scale (already folded into weight) and ideally the 2× maxpool directly into the convT epilogue: since maxpool kernel=2 evenly divides the output in D/H/W, each output position only contributes to one pooled cell — scatter-add into the pooled output buffer using `tl.atomic_max` after applying the bias, eliminating the full convT output materialization (256MB → 32MB).
- Then a tiny second kernel does GAP+clamp over PD·PH·PW≈14k elements per (N,C). This collapses 3 kernels into 2 and removes the dominant cuDNN call.
